deep.reconstruction:
This is not a mathematical derivation. It is an outline of lecture notes on elementary hydrostatics, apparently for a physics course. It continues the previous page, which covered incompressible fluids, areometers, pressure proportional to depth, and communicating vessels. It leads into the next page, on compressible fluids and Mariotte's (Boyle's) law. There are no formulas on the page. Below I put the content into modern notation; anything the page does not literally say is marked as mine.

Section C. All points of the same horizontal plane in a fluid at rest have the same pressure. In modern terms, p = p0 + rho*g*h, where h is the depth below the free surface. So p depends only on h. [Equation mine.]

Definition of pressure. "Druck" is the pressure force exerted on the unit of the pressure surface: p = F/A. The next clause is hard to read.
- Reading (i): "also ... die Druckfläche überflüssig". Since pressure is force per unit area, the size of the surface drops out.
- Reading (ii), close to the machine reading "u. d. Druckfläche u. Schwerp.": the total force on a plane surface is proportional to its area and to the depth of its centroid, F = rho*g*A*h_centroid. [Formula mine.] This is the standard textbook companion to the previous page's statement that pressure is proportional to area and depth.

Applications ("Anwendungen").
- 1a) Determination of specific gravity, using Archimedes' principle and the areometers and hydrostatic balance of the previous page.
- 1b) Something is said about the solid bodies bounding the fluid in nature; it may say they are made "superfluous". This is Archimedes' principle applied to bodies wholly immersed in a fluid, with buoyant force rho_fluid*g*V. Example: a balloon rises because it simultaneously displaces air whose weight exceeds its own. It rises while rho_air*V*g exceeds its weight. [Inequality mine.]
- 2) The hydraulic press and its extension. Pascal's principle gives F2/F1 = A2/A1. [Formula mine.]

Afterwards come absolute versus relative pressure (pressure difference, p - p0), and a remark connecting wall stress with friction (reading uncertain).
errors: No mathematical errors are possible to identify: the page states standard hydrostatic facts without derivation. The physical statements as readable (equal pressure on horizontal planes, pressure as force per unit area, buoyancy explanation of balloon ascent, hydraulic press) are correct.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine syllabus outline of elementary hydrostatics (Stevin, Pascal, Archimedes, hydraulic press). It is of minor biographical interest, as it shows Riemann preparing or recording elementary physics teaching material. It contains no new mathematics.

checkable.sympy: rho,g,h,p0=symbols('rho g h p0'); p=p0+rho*g*h; diff(p,symbols('x'))==0
checkable.asserts: Hydrostatic pressure depends only on depth h, not on horizontal position x.

checkable.sympy: rho,g,a,b,d,theta,s,t=symbols('rho g a b d theta s t',positive=True); F=integrate(integrate(rho*g*(d+s*sin(theta)),(s,0,a)),(t,0,b)); simplify(F-rho*g*a*b*(d+a*sin(theta)/2))==0
checkable.asserts: The force on a submerged inclined rectangle equals rho*g*A*(depth of its centroid).
Hydraulic press: with equal pressure the forces scale as the piston areas.
Archimedes: the buoyant force equals the weight of the displaced fluid.

transcription_corrections: Line 3 continuation: 'also u. d. Druckfläche u. Schwerp.' may instead read 'also ... d. Druckfläche überflüssig' (the size of the area drops out). The word read as 'Schwerp.' looks more like 'überflüssig' ('übflüssig'); the same word recurs in 1b ('... begrenzenden Körper überflüssig gemacht').
'1) specifisches Gewicht Bestimmungen zustandekommt' is more likely '1) a) specifische Gewichtsbestimmungen zurückgeführt' (sub-item a, matching the following 'b)').
'b) in der Natur der festen die Flüssigk. bei begrenzenden Körper' probably reads 'b) ist d. Natur der festen die Flüssigkeit begrenzenden Körper ... gemacht'.
'Ballon Steigung – indem er f. d. ... Massen gleichzeitig die Luft verdrängt' is roughly 'Ballon Steigung – indem er ... (Körper ...) gleichzeitig die Luft verdrängt'. The middle word is uncertain.
'2) hydraulische Presse [?] Erweiterung' is confirmed as 'hydraulische Presse, Erweiterung'.
'Zur Wandspannung ... Reibung': the last word is plausibly 'Reibung'; the middle word is uncertain (possibly 'Zur Wandspannung ... statt Reibung').
